bug_semantics: Scriban's object-to-string rendering recursively formats every ScriptObject member value without tracking object identity. With the default ObjectRecursionLimit of 0 (unlimited), a ScriptObject that directly or indirectly contains itself repeatedly re-enters ObjectToString until the CLR throws an uncatchable StackOverflowException, terminating the host process and enabling denial of service wherever an attacker can influence the rendered object graph.
flaw_origin: cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e is the smallest real introducer: it added the ScriptObject-specific pretty-print branch to ScriptValueConverter.ToString and the recursive call result.Append(ToString(span, keyPair.Value)). Its parent only handled ScriptObject through the generic IEnumerable path and did not recursively extract a KeyValuePair's Value, so the advisory PoC's self-referential ScriptObject path was absent. Later commits moved/refactored the formatter; a9affb64614358838aba16f28acb198f914e586d added an opt-in recursion guard but explicitly initialized ObjectRecursionLimit to 0, preserving the vulnerable default rather than introducing the already-existing recursion.
evidence: Advisory mechanism and boundary: https://github.com/scriban/scriban/security/advisories/GHSA-grr9-747v-xvcp gives the self-referential ScriptObject PoC (template {{ a }}, a["self"] = a), explains that ObjectRecursionLimit defaults to unlimited and the resulting StackOverflowException terminates the process, lists 6.5.8 as affected and 6.6.0 as patched, and recommends a safe nonzero default. https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pprh-wgqr-2mmx identifies this as CVE-2026-74794 and describes Scriban before 6.6.0 as affected.

BIC patch: in the validated clone, `git show --format=fuller --patch cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e -- src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptValueConverter.cs` shows the new ScriptObject branch and exact recursive sink `result.Append(ToString(span, keyPair.Value));`; the commit is dated 2016-04-19 and titled `Fix pretty print object ScriptObject and ScriptArray, dump objects with {...} and [...]`.

Independent origin cross-checks: `git log -L 30,52:src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptValueConverter.cs cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e` attributes the entire ScriptObject branch to cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e, while `git log --all -S'result.Append(ToString(span, keyPair.Value))' -- src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptValueConverter.cs src/Textamina.Scriban/Runtime/ScriptValueConverter.cs` finds cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e as the addition and 55a6d61fb656e87a49bbe49334236be558c5d3a1 only as its later removal/move during refactoring.

Direct parent absence: `git show 790f00752e7b7392f2849452f37345852f313634:src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptValueConverter.cs` has no ScriptObject-specific branch and no recursive extraction of a ScriptObject member's KeyValuePair.Value. `git show cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e` shows that branch as a pure addition over that immediate parent. Thus the advisory PoC's self-reference is not followed in the parent but is followed after the BIC.

Lifecycle cross-check: `git show a9affb64614358838aba16f28acb198f914e586d` shows that the 2021 guard checked `ObjectRecursionLimit != 0` but its constructor assignment was `ObjectRecursionLimit=0` and its documentation said `Default is 0, no limit`; this was an optional mitigation with an unsafe default, not the first recursive formatter. `git blame a6fe6074199e5c04f4d29dc8d8e652b24d33e3e4^ -- src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptObject.cs` traces the modern recursive member-value call through later refactors, while the -L/-S checks recover cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e as its actual origin.

Direct fix: `git show --format=fuller --patch a6fe6074199e5c04f4d29dc8d8e652b24d33e3e4` changes the TemplateContext constructor from `ObjectRecursionLimit = 0` to `ObjectRecursionLimit = 20` and updates the documented default. `git log --all -S'ObjectRecursionLimit = 20' -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` returns only this commit, so it is the direct closing change for the advisory's object-rendering path.

Version boundary: `git tag --contains a6fe6074199e5c04f4d29dc8d8e652b24d33e3e4` begins at 6.6.0 and excludes 6.5.8; `git log 6.5.8..6.6.0` includes the fix. `git for-each-ref --contains=cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e --sort=creatordate refs/tags` begins with v0.1.0 and includes every later line through 6.5.8, establishing that repository history contains the flawed formatter long before the advisory's currently enumerated affected release and that 6.6.0 is the first fixed release boundary.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e` shows author and committer Alexandre Mutel <alexandre_mutel@live.com>, one parent 790f00752e7b7392f2849452f37345852f313634, and only the ordinary subject line. The commit object contains no Co-authored-by, Generated-with, Copilot, bot identity, or other AI marker. AI markers on later fix/refactor commits were not used for the verdict.
reasoning: The vulnerability is the unbounded recursive formatting edge first introduced when cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e began descending into each ScriptObject member value. Its immediate parent does not contain that edge, so parent absence is directly established; later moves and the 2021 optional guard are not BICs. a6fe6074199e5c04f4d29dc8d8e652b24d33e3e4 closes the default attack path by making the existing recursion limit nonzero, and tag containment places that fix in 6.6.0 but not 6.5.8. The BIC commit object is a normal human-authored 2016 commit with no AI attribution or bot identity, so under the required BIC-only rule the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
